newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank to keep interbank rates high.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank to keep interbank rates high.

text.p: Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on wednesday the central bank will keep interbank rates high to attract capital inflow.
Rerngchai told a seminar he believed a Thai overnight interbank rate of five to seven percent was too low.
"The liquidity level in the market is high due to the government pension and provident funds which enter the market, totalling 70 billion baht and (which) will reach 100 billion," he said.
The governor said the central bank will move to absorb any excessive liquidity and maintain high interbank rates.
"If the interbank rate is too low, there will be no incentive for capital inflow as the interest rate differential is too narrow," he said.
The overnight interbank rate stood at 9.50-10.00 percent on Wednesday morning against 5.75-6.00 percent on Monday and 9.75-10.00 percent on Tuesday.
Rerngchai said the central bank will not have any problem adjusting market liquidity as most of the bonds it auctioned out in the past two weeks were short-term.
"The central bank bonds used to absorb excessive liquidity mostly carried one month maturity. We can roll over the amount. We believe it is appropriate to the market situation," he said.
The Bank of Thailand recently sharply increased its weekly one-month bond auctions to mop up liquidity boosted by the launch of government pension and provident funds this week.
